reason: This passage (Exodus 1:15-22) presents the exact opposite moral dynamic. The elite (Pharaoh) issues an immoral command to commit infanticide against Hebrew newborns. The regular people (Hebrew midwives, Shifrah and Puah) 'feared God' (וַתִּירֶאןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִים) and refused to obey the ruler's evil decree ('וְלֹא עָשׂוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֲלֵיהֶן מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם'). Instead, they preserved the children. The text then explicitly states that God rewarded the midwives ('וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת'), while the Hebrew population flourished. The moral hierarchy presented is inverted from the statement: the regular people demonstrate superior moral agency and are divinely approved, while the elite are condemned for attempting genocide.
